target_customer: Consumer facing businesses with high volume phone sales and support, such as retail, home services and insurance
problem: Inbound and outbound phone sales rely on costly human agents and seasonal hiring; Simple AI voice agents answer calls, know product catalogs and close orders.
business_model: Outcome based pricing for voice and omnichannel AI sales agents

founders.name: Catheryn Li
education: MIT, degrees in computer science and math
founders.background_notes: Four years at YC leading the software team for Startup School, YC Library and Co-Founder Matching.

technical_complexity.rationale: Low latency voice pipeline with catalog grounding and telephony integrations; hard parts are latency and reliability.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with Five9, Genesys and Salesforce add stickiness, but voice agent platforms are widely available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Many voice agent startups were active by 2025 and 2026 with large raises (for example Vapi $50M Series B), so the wedge was crowded.

market_need_then: Omaha Steaks reportedly cut seasonal hiring from 5,000 to 692 and call abandonment from 16% to 3% per the company case study (company claim). The founders' consumer phone assistant led to the Omaha Steaks interest.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and customer centric, 'Revenue made Simple'

branding.community_and_virality: Earlier consumer products 'Simple AI, a better Siri' and an AI phone assistant app gave awareness; a customer CEO prank called his COO using the consumer app per a YC interview summary

brand_strength.rationale: Name is easy and fits the outcome pricing pitch but is generic and on a prefix domain; consumer app was a distribution wedge.

outcome_analysis: Simple AI began with consumer assistants and moved into enterprise voice sales agents, landing Omaha Steaks and other named customers. It raised a $14M seed in February 2026 led by First Harmonic. Competition from voice agent platforms is intense but it shows early enterprise traction.
notes: Business Wire page returned 403 on direct fetch; the round is confirmed by the company blog, Pulse 2.0 and Business Wire listing via search. The pivot from consumer assistant to enterprise sales has no source date. No dated 2024 competitors found; named competitors' funding is from 2026 sources. Investors beyond the lead come from the CEO blog via search summary.
